There are a lot of people who are not as healthy as they wish to be. I have two things to talk about, what's going on in your brain and how you should take action.

Brain:

The receptors in our brain that deliver happy juice to our body are adjustable. Naturally, they are wired to go off when humans move their bodies, have sex, among other things. What happens when you start to live unhealthy (for example overeat or overdrink) is that those receptors stop reacting to the "intended" joys of life and start to only react to the unhealthy habits. So the receptors that previously activated when you learned something or when you ran in the woods, only go off when you drink alcohol for example.

This is one reason why bad habits are so hard to break, because people don't realize (or don't want to wait) that their receptors need time to adjust to their new lifestyle, in order for the mind and body to be happy with it.

Taking steps:

When you want to live more healthy, take small steps. You can have a vision of how you want things to be, but don't let that be your goal. Always let your goal be achievable and perhaps most importantly, sustainable. When you take a step to be more healthy (and keep it), you'll notice that things start to get a little easier. You have a little more energy. You feel a bit stronger. Things don't feel so hard anymore. That's when you take the next step, and things feel even more energetic and strong.

This is how good health snowballs. Don't try to live a perfectly healthy live right from the start, because you will almost certainly fail. Take small steps, because you'll realize that those small steps makes the next steps easier and not even hard to do.

Before and after:

I used to eat loads of sugary stuff (mostly chocolate) and almost never exercise. Now I've completely stopped eating sugary products. The thing is, it's not even hard at all to not eat sugary stuff now. The hard part isn't not-starting, the hard part is stopping when you're already started.

I've also started to work out. Not much, but it's regular (every other day). Again, this doesn't feel so difficult to maintain. I pretty much never get that feeling of not-wanting-to before a workout, it isn't a chore anymore. Right now working out feels okay. It feels a little good to move your body and work it, but it also feels a bit meh because it's exhausting. The most important discovery I've realized is how important it is to have a pre-workout meal. You can't workout if your body doesn't have energy.
When striving to be more healthy, focus on one very small step at a time. You'll notice things will start to snowball. [personal tips inside]
